title: SWE-Critix: Post-Training Generalist Verifiers for Assessing Coding-Agent Trajectories
title_zh: SWE-Critix：面向编码智能体轨迹评估的后训练通用验证器

paragraphs.en: Coding agents are increasingly deployed for end-to-end software engineering tasks, where a readily available oracle evaluator that defines the success criteria is often absent. This motivates verifications for coding agents that can reliably judge and explain their behavior. However, verification is non-trivial as coding agents are increasingly capable of solving long-horizon software engineering tasks. Their execution trajectories can be extremely long, containing hundreds of iterative interactions with code repositories and external tools. Existing verifiers either rely on general-purpose LLMs without specialized training or train dedicated critics that predominantly focus on producing scalar rewards, highlighting the relatively limited exploration of training-based generalist verification. We introduce SWE-Critix , a post-training pipeline for training generalist verifiers of coding-agent trajectories. Given a task and its execution trajectory, the learned verifier predicts the completion label and generates a natural-language analysis that explains its judgment. Our pipeline combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with reinforcement learning (RL) and trains a series of 30B models on trajectories from CodeForge-Preview. On a held-out test set, SWE-Critix improves classification accuracy from 57% for the base Qwen3-30B-A3B reasoning model to 66% after SFT and 78% after RL. We release our models, datasets, and training code to facilitate further research.

paragraphs.en: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have enabled a shift from code generation toward autonomous coding agents that can interact with environments to solve complex software engineering tasks. Rather than producing one-shot code snippets, coding agents can inspect repositories, edit files, execute commands, run tests, interpret feedback, and iteratively refine their solutions through interactions with external tools [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] . This agentic paradigm has substantially expanded the scope of automated programming from isolated function synthesis to repository-level issue resolution [ 4 ] and long-horizon software development tasks [ 5 , 6 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 大型语言模型（LLM）的最新进展使得研究重点从代码生成转向了能够与环境交互以解决复杂软件工程任务的自主编码智能体。 与仅生成单次代码片段不同，编码智能体能够检查代码库、编辑文件、执行命令、运行测试、解读反馈，并通过与外部工具的交互迭代优化其解决方案 [ 1 , 2 , 3 ] 。 这种智能体范式显著拓展了自动化编程的范畴，从孤立的函数合成扩展到了代码库级别的故障解决 [ 4 ] 以及长期软件开发任务 [ 5 , 6 ] 。

paragraphs.en: As coding agents become more capable and autonomous, reliably verifying their execution trajectories (i.e., step-by-step record of an agent solving a task) becomes increasingly important. In realistic end-to-end tasks, the criteria for successful completion are often not explicitly specified by a readily available ground-truth oracle. A verifier is therefore needed to determine whether an agent has accomplished the task and, when it fails, identify the causes of failure. However, such verification is challenging because coding-agent trajectories can contain hundreds of interleaved user inputs, environment feedback, and model responses, making them substantially more difficult to inspect than a one-shot model response. For instance, trajectories for tasks in LoLBench [ 6 ] span 53–532 turns and contain millions of tokens on average.
paragraphs.zh: 随着编码智能体能力越来越强且自主性越来越高，可靠地验证其执行轨迹（即智能体完成任务时的逐步记录）变得日益重要。 在真实的端到端任务中，成功完成的标准通常无法通过现成的真实值预言机明确指定。 因此，需要一种验证机制来判断智能体是否完成了任务，并在其失败时识别失败的原因。 然而，这种验证颇具挑战，因为编码智能体的轨迹可能包含数百个交错的用户输入、环境反馈和模型响应，使其比单次模型响应更难检查。 例如，LoLBench [6] 中任务的执行轨迹通常包含 53 至 532 轮交互，平均包含数百万个词元。

paragraphs.en: To address the challenge, existing work have proposed different techniques from two orthogonal dimensions: verification target and method , as summarized in Table I . The former distinguishes whether a verifier evaluates only the agent’s final outcome (e.g., the submitted patch) or also examines the process to detect undesirable intermediate behaviors. The latter distinguishes whether a verifier is constructed with or without training. Training-free methods directly employ general-purpose LLMs or conventional rule-based judges, whereas training-based methods learn dedicated critics, which can be further characterized by whether they produce scalar rewards or richer natural-language assessments.
paragraphs.zh: 为应对这一挑战，现有研究从两个正交维度——验证目标和验证方法——提出了不同的技术，如表 I 所示。 前者区分了验证器是仅评估智能体的最终结果（例如提交的补丁），还是同时检查过程以检测不良的中间行为。 后者区分了验证器是否经过训练而构建。 无需训练的方法直接使用通用大型语言模型或传统的基于规则的评判者，而基于训练的方法则会学习专门的批评者，这些批评者还可根据它们输出标量奖励还是更丰富的自然语言评估来进一步分类。

paragraphs.en: This taxonomy reveals that training-based, process-oriented generalist verification remains relatively underexplored. To fill the gap, we propose SWE-Critix (Figure 1 ), a post-training pipeline that combines supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning (RL) to train a generalist trajectory verifier. Given a task and its execution trajectory, the learned verifier not only determines whether the task has been successfully completed but also justifies the rationale underlying its judgment. Compared with the two existing approaches in this category, SWE-Critix differs from them in terms of verification target (planning phase [ 30 ] vs. whole trajectory), annotation strategy (per-step dense labeling [ 31 ] vs. differential analysis), scale (2–8K training samples and 4–8B models [ 30 , 31 ] vs. 119K and 30B), learning algorithms (DPO [ 30 ] vs. GRPO), and reward design (process reward [ 31 ] vs. outcome reward).

paragraphs.en: Figure 1 shows the post-training pipeline of SWE-Critix , which learns an LLM (i.e., a generalist verifier) for evaluating coding-agent trajectories. The verifier takes an issue-solving trajectory as input and determines whether the issue has been successfully resolved. Before making the binary judgment, the verifier produces a chain-of-thought (CoT) rationale that casually infers its decision (Figure 1 -Application).
paragraphs.zh: 图 1 展示了 SWE-Critix 的训练后流程，该流程会学习一个 LLM（即通用验证器），用于评估编码智能体的执行轨迹。 该验证器以问题求解轨迹作为输入，并判断问题是否已成功解决。 在做出二元判断之前，验证器会生成一条思维链（CoT）推理过程，以非正式的方式解释其决策依据（图 1 - 应用）。

paragraphs.en: To train the verifier, SWE-Critix first applies a more capable teacher LLM to review a pair of successful and failed trajectories that address the same issue. Through differential analysis, the teacher summarizes the respective procedures, mistake patterns, and key factors leading to the success or failure of each trajectory (Figure 1 -CoT Annotation). These summaries are then incorporated into a small amount of SFT training samples, providing supervision for the base model to learn the reasoning process underlying trajectory evaluation (Figure 1 -SFT). Finally, RL is applied to a substantial number of samples without CoT annotations, where unit-testing results are used as ground truth for computing the reward signal (Figure 1 -RL).
paragraphs.zh: 为了训练验证器，SWE-Critix 首先使用一个能力更强的教师 LLM 来审查一对解决同一问题的成功和失败轨迹。 通过差异分析，该教师总结了各自的过程、错误模式以及导致每条轨迹成功或失败的关键因素（图 1 - CoT 标注）。 随后，这些总结被整合到少量 SFT 训练样本中，为基模型提供监督，使其能够学习轨迹评估背后的推理过程（图 1 - SFT）。 最后，将 RL 应用于大量没有 CoT 标注的样本，其中单元测试结果被用作计算奖励信号的真实参考（图 1 - RL）。

paragraphs.en: It has been widely acknowledged that generating a CoT before providing the final answer significantly improves the performance of LLMs to resolve complex tasks [ 39 , 40 , 41 ] . To bootstrap the reasoning capabilities of our target verifier, SWE-Critix leverages a teacher LLM (GPT-5.5) to generate a structured CoT trace by comparatively analyzing each pair of successful and failed trajectories in the SFT set. We adopt this pairwise comparison approach based on prior findings that LLMs perform better in pairwise evaluations than in individual judgments [ 42 , 43 ] . We then post-process the generated CoTs to adapt them for pointwise judgment, which is the intended evaluation setting for the trained verifier. The prompt templates and more details are released on GitHub [ 33 ] . The resulting CoT trace of a trajectory includes a concise summary of its issue-resolving procedure, a characterization of mistake patterns based on a predefined taxonomy, and a causal summary of the factors contributing to the success or failure of the trajectory. We apply CoT annotation only to the SFT set, which contains 10,390 trajectories and accounts for 8.7% of the training set.
paragraphs.zh: 人们普遍认为，在提供最终答案之前生成思考链（CoT），能显著提升大型语言模型（LLM）解决复杂任务的性能 [ 39 , 40 , 41 ] 。 为了启动目标验证器的推理能力，SWE-Critix 利用一个教师型 LLM（GPT-5.5），通过对比分析 SFT 集合中每对成功与失败的轨迹，生成结构化的思考链（CoT）痕迹。 我们采用这种成对比较方法，是基于先前发现：LLM 在成对评估中的表现优于单独判断 [ 42 , 43 ] 。 随后，我们对生成的思考链（CoT）进行后处理，以适配逐点判断——这正是训练后的验证器所设计的评估场景。 提示模板及更多细节已发布在 GitHub 上 [ 33 ] 。 某条轨迹最终生成的思考链（CoT）痕迹包括：其问题解决流程的简要总结、基于预定义分类法对错误模式的描述，以及导致该轨迹成功或失败的因素的因果总结。 我们仅对 SFT 集合应用思考链（CoT）标注，该集合包含 10,390 条轨迹，占训练集总量的 8.7%。

paragraphs.en: We present the results in Table II . The results reveal a clear progression from general-purpose language modeling to specialized trajectory verification. The base Qwen3 MoE model exhibits a strong bias toward predicting trajectories as correct, as its negative recall is nearly zero across all subsets. It also has limited instruction following capability on this task. We observed that 9.6% of its responses do not adhere to the required output format, preventing reliable extraction of the predicted judgments. SFT substantially alleviates both issues. All responses produced by π SFT \pi_{\mathrm{SFT}} strictly follow the instructions required by the prompt, and the model becomes considerably less biased toward positive predictions. Further RL training yields another significant improvement, increasing accuracy from 66% after SFT to 78% on the overall test set. These results suggest that SFT primarily addresses the base model’s strong positive bias, while subsequent RL further strengthens its discriminative capability by recovering positive recall from 67% to 85% without substantially sacrificing negative recall.

paragraphs.en: 2. Training Methods : It remains an open question whether RL alone is sufficient to train an effective verifier. paragraphs.en: Prior work proposing verifiers for reviewing coding-agent executions can be classified into two major categories depending on whether a specialized verification model is trained. One is training-free verification, where an evaluator agent uses general-purpose LLMs to assess coding agent executions through test generation [ 7 , 9 ] , rubric-based grading [ 10 , 11 , 12 ] , verification scaling [ 8 ] , metamorphic relations [ 16 ] , failure attribution [ 13 ] , or anti-pattern detection [ 14 , 17 , 18 , 15 ] . Another major category is training-based verification, where a specialized critic is trained to evaluate trajectories using different learning paradigms such as TD learning [ 25 , 26 ] , autoregressive next-token prediction [ 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 , 28 , 10 , 30 , 29 , 31 ] , multi-label classification [ 27 ] , DPO [ 30 ] , Bradley-Terry [ 24 ] , and policy gradient [ 28 , 31 ] .
paragraphs.zh: 此前提出用于审查编码智能体执行过程的验证器的工作，可以根据是否训练了专门的验证模型，分为两大类。 一类是无训练验证，其中评估智能体使用通用大型语言模型，通过测试生成 [ 7 , 9 ]、基于评分标准的打分 [ 10 , 11 , 12 ]、验证扩展 [ 8 ]、形态变化关系 [ 16 ]、失败归因 [ 13 ] 或反模式检测 [ 14 , 17 , 18 , 15 ] 来评估编码智能体的执行过程。 另一大类是基于训练的验证，其中会训练一个专门的批评者，利用不同的学习范式（如 TD 学习 [ 25 , 26 ]、自回归的下一个词预测 [ 19 , 20 , 21 , 22 , 23 , 28 , 10 , 30 , 29 , 31 ]、多标签分类 [ 27 ]、DPO [ 30 ]、Bradley-Terry [ 24 ] 和策略梯度 [ 28 , 31 ]）来评估执行轨迹。

paragraphs.en: In this paper, we proposed a post-training pipeline SWE-Critix that integrates SFT with RL to learn a process-level generalist verifier for assessing coding-agent trajectories. Preliminary experiments on coding-agent trajectories from CodeForge-Preview demonstrate a substantial improvement in the model’s discriminative ability.
